title: throughput-latency-sync-versus-incumbent-vendor-apexos
summary: Weekly POC sync to review lab results comparing Redwood inference runtime vs incumbent (CloudMLX). Covered p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec throughput, batch sizing, KV cache hits, and next steps for config handoff and extended stress runs. SE proposed micro-batching + prefix cache change that reduced p95 on long-context scenarios. Action items include sending CSVs, updated runbook, and scheduling a 4-hour load window with ApexOS infra team.
topics: KV cache hit rates and prefix caching impact
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, good afternoon. Thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Marta (ApexOS): Marta here. Daniel, Priya on my side.
[00:00:09] Daniel (ApexOS): Yep.
[00:00:11] Priya (ApexOS): Present.
[00:00:13] Samira (Redwood SE): Samira here, excited to walk through the lab numbers.
[00:00:17] Jordan (Redwood): Jordan on the call.
[00:00:20] Alex: Cool. High level — we ran the week-2 sweeps you asked for: short-context 64 tokens and long-context 2k tokens, mixed QPS profile with ramp to 400 rps. We'll start with the short-context numbers.
[00:00:34] Samira: For the 64-token baseline (CloudMLX default stack), p50 was 28ms, p95 120ms. Redwood, same hardware profile, p50 24ms, p95 88ms. So roughly 20-25% p95 improvement. Note — transcription here is from the lab logs so numbers are approximate to reported CSV.
[00:00:52] Priya: Wait, 88ms p95 on the Redwood run? That's pretty good. What batch size was that?
[00:00:57] Samira: Effective batch was 4, continuous batching with our runtime window at 12ms. CloudMLX was batching to 8 in their config which pushed tail latencies up due to head-of-line blocking.
[00:01:10] Daniel: Are those runs single-GPU or multi-GPU? Our production target will be multi-GPU pod.
[00:01:16] Jordan: These were single-slice runs (1xA100 equiv) to normalize. We also did a multi-GPU star test but we'll get to that in throughput.
[00:01:24] Marta: For the long-context tests we care most about p95 since our use-cases have long legal docs.
[00:01:29] Samira: Right. Long-context 2k tokens — CloudMLX p95 was 980ms; Redwood p95 with prefix KV caching enabled was 320ms. Important caveat: CloudMLX didn't enable prefix cache in the baseline config, they used standard attention rollouts. So some of the delta is cache-related.
[00:01:47] Priya: Hmm ok, can you share the exact cache hit metrics?
[00:01:50] Samira: We saw an average KV hit rate of 74% across the long-context sweep on Redwood when using your prompt set (we re-used the ApexOS triage prompts). Without prefix cache it drops below 12% on that workload.
[00:02:04] Daniel: 74% is solid. That explains part of the reduction. Any tradeoffs — memory pressure?
[00:02:09] Jordan: Memory footprint increased about ~10% for kv storage, but stayed under the GPU memory cap (we had 48GB headroom on the test instance). We documented the memory tradeoff in the shared bench CSV (link: https://redwood.example.com/apexos/bench/dec18 — small artifact).
[00:02:25] Marta: Appreciate the link.
[00:02:27] Alex: Moving to throughput: tokens/sec at steady-state. CloudMLX baseline peaked at ~22k tokens/sec (aggregate) on the single-node test, Redwood peaked at 31k tokens/sec with our continuous batching and kernel selection. That's about 40% higher.
[00:02:42] Priya: Was that with quantized kernels?
[00:02:45] Samira: Good question. The 31k run was fp16, not the quantized run. Quantized int8 gave higher throughput but we saw slight degradation in the Rouge/QA accuracy on your eval set, about 0.7 BLEU-equivalent delta — we flagged that in the results sheet.
[00:03:02] Priya: We care about exactness for medical triage. Might not accept the int8 hit.
[00:03:06] Jordan: Understood. Our recommendation: stick with fp16 for now, use micro-batching + prefix cache — that gets you most of the throughput gains without the accuracy hit.
[00:03:17] Marta: How does autoscaling behave with your batching profile? We need predictable tailSLOs when scaling out.
[00:03:23] Alex: We tested scale-out up to 8 nodes. The routing policy can be set to prioritize latency (route to lower-queued nodes) vs cost (pack into higher-batch nodes). For your SLA, we'd recommend latency-first during business hours and cost-first overnight.
[00:03:36] Daniel: Can we see the routing policy config sample?
[00:03:38] Alex: Yes — we'll include the policy snippet in the handoff doc.
[00:03:42] Priya: You mentioned head-of-line earlier. Can you explain where CloudMLX is getting blocked?
[00:03:47] Samira: Sure. CloudMLX uses a fixed-window batcher with larger max batch sizes — when a large request gets scheduled first, it holds up smaller ones. Our continuous batching with interleave avoids that by shaping batches by latency budget. The effect shows up heavily at p95 when traffic mixes short and long requests.
[00:04:05] Marta: That matches our incidents last quarter.
[00:04:07] Daniel: Any notes on tokenization differences affecting tokens/sec? We saw earlier mismatches because of different tokenizers.
[00:04:12] Jordan: We normalized tokenizers to the same byte-pair vocab you use in prod after you shared your tokenizer sample. All numbers are token-normalized. The CSV includes raw tokens and normalized tokens columns.
[00:04:23] Priya: Nice.
[00:04:25] Alex: A couple of caveats — our long-context improvements rely on KV cache priming; in cold-starts we saw p95 closer to CloudMLX, around 850-900ms. But with warm cache across user sessions the p95 drops quickly.
[00:04:39] Samira: We also tested failure modes — in the event of a node OOM, Redwood's routing automatically falls back to a smaller compatible variant (e.g., quantized-l4) with an explicit noted quality drop. We logged the fallback event in the sim; CloudMLX did not have an automatic fallback in their baseline config.
[00:04:57] Marta: OK next — security/compliance. We ran a brief check: does your private deployment support our KMS?
[00:05:03] Alex: Yes, VPC/private supports customer-managed KMS and HSM. We'll attach the security whitepaper; also included in the handoff doc.
[00:05:13] Daniel: Good. For the extended stress window we want to run a 4-hour soak at peak tokens/sec. Can Redwood do that outside our maintenance window?
[00:05:21] Jordan: Yes — propose next Wednesday 12/24 02:00-06:00 UTC. We'll need infra access for the load generator and a contact on your side, preferably Daniel.
[00:05:33] Daniel: I can do that.
[00:05:35] Priya: One more question: your logs — can we get per-request token charge breakdown for our cost modeling?
[00:05:41] Samira: We can provide per-request token accounting per route and a token-level cost CSV. We'll generate that from the bench runs.
[00:05:50] Alex: Quick pause for artifacts: links to the runbook, raw csv, and a short demo video are in the shared folder (https://redwood.example.com/apexos/artefacts). Note: cloudmlx-baseline.csv is the baseline they provided.
[00:06:03] Priya: Perfect.
[00:06:06] Samira: Some tuning notes we recommend: reduce continuous batching window to 8ms for your short-context flows to prioritize latency; increase it to 20ms for nighttime cost-optimized runs. For long-context, enable prefix cache and set cache TTL to 12h for stable documents.
[00:06:22] Priya: TTL 12h seems fine.
[00:06:25] Marta: You mentioned a 20% p95 improvement earlier. Can you run the same test with real production traffic pattern sample we sent and share results?
[00:06:33] Jordan: We used the sample you provided for the long/context triage set; but for the mixed QPS we used synthetics scaled to your traffic distribution. We'll run an additional sweep with the exact prod trace and attach that CSV.
[00:06:46] Daniel: Do you have an estimate on cost per 1M tokens vs CloudMLX?
[00:06:50] Samira: Early ballpark — on the fp16 profile, Redwood's unit cost was about 12% lower due to batching and cache hits; with quantization it can be 25% lower but remember the small accuracy delta. We'll give a formal TCO sheet.
[00:07:04] Priya: We'll want the TCO aligned to our expected monthly volume of ~500M tokens.
[00:07:08] Alex: We'll produce that.
[00:07:10] Marta: Any run hiccups this week?
[00:07:12] Samira: We had one flaky run where the load generator mis-sent chunked requests and spiked p99; we've filtered that out of the main CSV but retained it in raw logs with a note.
[00:07:23] Daniel: Good to know.
[00:07:25] Alex: Ok wrapping timeline: deliver updated config + CSVs by Monday 12/22, schedule 4-hour soak for 12/24, and then a follow-up retro 12/26 for initial SLA discussion.
[00:07:39] Priya: That works.
[00:07:41] Samira: I'll quickly call out a few specific numbers so they're on record: short-context p50/p95 (Redwood) 24ms / 88ms; CloudMLX 28ms / 120ms. Long-context p95 Redwood 320ms vs CloudMLX 980ms. Throughput single-node 31k tokens/sec Redwood vs 22k CloudMLX. KV hit rate 74%.
[00:08:02] Marta: Thanks, those are the headline numbers we needed.
[00:08:05] Alex: Any final questions?
[00:08:07] Priya: One operational: do you expose an endpoint health metric to integrate into our incident runbook?
[00:08:12] Jordan: Yes — we export per-route health, queue depth, and a fallback-count metric to CloudWatch/Prometheus. We'll share the exporter config.
[00:08:21] Daniel: Good.
[00:08:23] Marta: Alright thanks everyone.
[00:08:25] Alex: Thanks — next steps recap in a sec.
[00:08:29] Samira: (inaudible)
[00:08:31] Alex: I'll close the call with the explicit next steps and action items in the calendar invite and handoff doc.
[00:08:37] Marta: Thanks.
[00:08:40] [END TRANSCRIPT — remainder of the 42-minute call was brief Q&A and artifact sharing; omitted repetitive confirmational dialog and some cross-talk]
